neighbours.label: the word piece that follows a word-initial 'Am' / 'Amh' in names (Am·har·ic, Amh·ara, Am·os, Am·ida, Am·asa); not 'Am…' words that are a single token (Amanda, America)
fire: The radio station broadcasts in Amharic every evening.
The lesson today is taken from the book of Amos.
Farmers in the Amhara highlands grow teff and barley.
The temple hall holds a large wooden statue of Amida.
The farm was founded by Amasa Stone before the war.
She learned to read Amharic script from her grandmother.
The film Amadeus won several awards that year.
Pilgrims travel to the golden temple at Amritsar each spring.
quiet: The radio station broadcasts in Swahili every evening.
The lesson today is taken from the book of Micah.
Farmers in the Oromia highlands grow teff and barley.
The temple hall holds a large wooden statue of Kannon.
The farm was founded by Amanda Stone before the war.
She learned to read Arabic script from her grandmother.
The film Casablanca won several awards in America that year.
Pilgrims travel to the golden temple at Kyoto each spring.

notes: Early layer: tested as a spelling unit. Probes: Amharic 1.03, Amos 1.01, Amasa 0.84, Amhara 0.81, Amida 0.77; lists of other Am-names were weaker (Amadeus 0.35, Amritsar 0.27); Amanda/America 0.00, Micah 0.11, Ramos/Thomas 0.02.
